tasks.task: Write a listing title and description

items.when: When a home needs a title and description built from its real features and rules
When the title is flat, to get several honest angles before picking one
When the description says cosy and stunning, to make each line true and easy to picture
When the listing is drafted, to read it as a guest and list what they would have to ask
When the listing is live, to check a guest can book the dates and price you meant today
When the listing lists features and never walks through the stay from the door inwards

tasks.task: Plan the listing photos and their order

items.when: Before the shoot, to list each shot and the guest question it answers
When photos exist, to plan which eight lead the gallery and what is missing
Before upload, to check sizes, file names and the caption for each photo
When a true photo needs straightening or brightening, without changing what the room is

tasks.task: Write the guest message set from booking to check-out

items.when: When setting up or rewriting the timed messages guests get around a stay
Before writing, to map each stage of the stay with what the guest worries about
When planning the series, to compare three ways to pace the messages and pick one
When guests write in another language and need the same message in theirs
When the set is drafted, to cut each message to what a tired traveller reads on a phone

tasks.task: Write a house guide for guests

items.when: When guests keep asking the same questions or a new home needs a guide before the first stay
When you have the real questions guests ask, to turn them into one clear page
When appliance or heating steps confuse guests, to rewrite them and test them read aloud
When the guide should be a printed handout checked page by page
When the guide is drafted, to read it as a guest arriving late and find what is missing

tasks.task: Draft replies to a batch of guest questions

items.when: When common questions need quick replies that match the house guide
When a question is unusual, to get a reply and notes on what to check before sending
When a reply reads cold, to try it warmer with the same facts
Before sending, to check no reply promises an early check-in or extra nobody agreed

tasks.task: Reply to guest reviews

items.when: When a guest has left a review, above all a tricky or negative one
When many reviews wait, to get a specific reply to each and a list of the risky ones
When reviews arrive every week, to hold risky ones back and flag repeat complaints
Before replying to a run of reviews, to rank what guests praise and complain about
When a reply sounds defensive, to try it calmer with the same facts
Before posting, to check the reply admits nothing untrue and promises nothing new
When a reply argues with the guest in front of every future guest who reads it

tasks.task: Handle a guest problem during a stay

items.when: When a stay goes wrong and the guest needs a fast, calm reply and a fix
Before replying, to read the message for urgency, safety and warning signs
When you want a warm reply, a fair fix and a note on who to tell
When the guest is furious, to try a reply that names the feeling first
Before a call with an angry guest, to plan calm questions and test what would settle it

tasks.task: Set out refund or cancellation options and their cost

items.when: When a guest asks for money back or the host is thinking about cancelling
When the decision is made, to write a clear yes, partial or no that leads with it
When the guest disputes the policy, to explain the booking terms in plain words
Before sending, to check the reply matches the policy and what the host agreed

tasks.task: Prepare a damage claim within the platform's time limit

items.when: When damage is found after check-out and a claim must go in on time
When the claim needs a dated timeline from messages, photos and cleaner notes
Before filing, to tie each item claimed to a dated photo, receipt or quote

tasks.task: Build a 12-month nightly price calendar

items.when: When a home needs a base rate with season, weekday and event layers the host approves
When a small hotel or B&B has several rooms and needs prices and a channel mix
When past bookings exist, to forecast busy and quiet weeks before setting layers
When the base rate is a guess, to test it against costs, rival prices and guest value
When a new rate goes live, to run one test you can undo and read the result

tasks.task: Set minimum stay, gap night and discount rules

items.when: When one and two night gaps sit empty or minimum stays are the same all year
When the rules must fit the price calendar and each platform's settings
When weekly, monthly and last-minute discounts need one matrix with limits
When a discount has run, to see the extra revenue against what it cost
Before a new discount, to find the deepest cut the margin per night allows

tasks.task: Review occupancy and revenue from a booking export

items.when: When a messy booking export must become occupancy, rate and revenue by month and channel
When the export has mixed dates, text numbers and duplicates, to clean it first
When you need revenue per channel after commission and service cost
When occupancy or rate fell, to rank the likely causes by evidence
Before the review goes to the owner, to find broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Work out the break-even and target nightly rate

items.when: When fees, cleaning and running costs must be set against nights sold
When you want the profit on one booking after every cost, and what moves it most
When the home carries a loan, to see how bad a year it can take before it stops earning
When the sums live in a spreadsheet, to find formula errors before the owner relies on them

tasks.task: Run the weekly revenue and calendar review

items.when: Each week for the 90-day pace check and gap sweep, and on the first working day of the month
When bookings on the books must be compared with the same point last year
When a host with many units wants the same numbers each week with a trend
When the sweep finds orphan nights, to decide which rule to relax

tasks.task: Launch a new listing or move to a new platform

items.when: When a host lists a home for the first time, adds a unit or joins a new platform
Before the first guest, to list the risks and the questions to ask an insurance broker
When the launch plan is drafted, to list how the first stays could go wrong
On launch day, to check the calendar is open and the price on the page is the one planned

tasks.task: Check local rules and registration before listing

items.when: Before a listing goes live, when a home is bought for short stays, or at each refresh
When a local rule changes, to see which house rules and settings it touches
When the check states a night cap or licence rule, to tie it to a dated official source

tasks.task: Run a booking through to check-out and turnover

items.when: On every new booking, to run messages, access, check-out and the clean in order
When each stay should feel the same, to write one page of checkable standards
When the cleaner needs a job card and a rule for what to do when a standard is missed
When linen and supplies run out, to set a simple restock rule for each
When the clean finds faults, to hand over each repair with access notes
When choosing a cleaning or laundry firm, to compare quotes and terms side by side

tasks.task: Write house rules and booking terms guests understand

items.when: When rules on noise, pets, parties and check-out need short, firm, friendly wording
When direct booking terms exist, to explain payment, cancelling and refunds in plain words
When the rules read like a threat, to try a version guests are glad to follow
When the rules are drafted, to cut them to one page a guest will read

tasks.task: Prepare a group booking handover sheet

items.when: When a group is confirmed, to check deposit and rate and list open requests and key dates
When the group lead needs their own messages on arrival, rooms and payment
When the group asks what happens if numbers drop or the date moves

tasks.task: Win direct bookings and repeat guests

items.when: When the host has a direct booking site, to see three first screens and pick one
When a B&B or small hotel must be found on local search and maps
When past guests gave consent to email, to write a short return-visit series
When add-ons such as late check-out could be sold, to pick ones to try with a small test
When the page or emails are drafted, to read them as a guest comparing with the platform

tasks.task: Report the month to the owner of a managed home

items.when: When a co-host must show the owner nights, rate and revenue net of fees and cleaning
When the month's income and costs must be set against last month
When the owner wants one page with the answer first and the decision needed
When the report is drafted, to read it as the owner and list what they would ask

tasks.task: Get the year's income and costs ready for the accountant

items.when: When a UK host files their own return, to list records, totals and accountant questions
When a year of costs must be sorted by home and by type
When tax bills come as a shock, to set a rule for what to put aside from each payout
Before the file goes, to check payouts by platform agree with the booking records

always.when: Before anything a guest reads goes live, to catch typos, wrong times and codes
When copy states a distance, an amenity or a platform rule, to tie it to a source or cut it

helpers.when: When the job is a direct booking push, social content or a seasonal campaign
When the listing needs a planned photo set, not just an order for the photos it has
When a home moves to long lets or needs tenant notices and a compliance log
When reviews across many platforms need a standing reply and recovery plan
When payouts, fees and cleaning costs must be reconciled for several homes each month
When the guide and messages must be properly translated for a main guest market

gaps: No library item writes a short-stay listing title and description or checks it against a platform's content rules
No library item builds a nightly price calendar with season, weekday and event layers for a single home
No library item sets minimum stay and gap night rules or sweeps a calendar for orphan nights
No library item works out occupancy, average daily rate and revenue per available night from a booking export
No library item checks booking pace against the same point last year
No library item checks short-let licence, registration, night cap and tourist tax rules for a named city
No library item writes a cleaning and turnover checklist or schedules cleaners against check-outs
No library item prepares a damage claim to a platform with photos, receipts and the deadline
No library item plans room and exterior photos for a property listing; the photo items are for products
No library item compares a home with a set of similar local listings on price and features
No tool guide covers channel managers, dynamic pricing tools or smart lock and messaging tools
No thinking lens covers revenue management or hotel-style hospitality
